\label{lemma-product-hypercoverings}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
If $K, L$ are hypercoverings of $X$, then
$K \times L$ is a hypercovering of $X$.

stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L1387 and Stage A logical fields: The levelwise fibre product of two hypercovers of X satisfies the matching-object local covering conditions by pullback permanence and product of coverings, hence is a hypercover. The product location is explicitly stated.

source_identity.original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-covering}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Let $k \geq 0$ be an integer.
Let $u : Z \to K_k$ be a covering
in $\text{SR}(\mathcal{C}, X)$.
Then there exists a morphism of hypercoverings
$f: L \to K$ such that $L_k \to K_k$
factors through $u$.

stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L1414 and Stage A logical fields: Any chosen covering of a specified level K_k can be absorbed by refining a hypercover K to L over K, with L_k→K_k factoring through the covering; the fixed level k and site fibre products remain.

source_identity.original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-covering-sheaf}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
Let $u : \mathcal{F} \to F(K_n)$ be a morphism
of presheaves which becomes surjective
on sheafification.
Then there exists a morphism of hypercoverings
$f: L \to K$ such that $F(f_n) : F(L_n) \to F(K_n)$
factors through $u$.

stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L1558 and Stage A logical fields: A presheaf map F→F(K_n) that is sheaf-locally surjective admits a semi-representable hypercover refinement making the level-n map factor through F. The sheafification condition and precise F(functor) direction are retained.
